title: Redwood POC weekly sync - cost econ review

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-17
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Samira (Redwood AE), Marcus (Redwood SE), Priya (Quantaco HoML), Tom (Quantaco Eng Lead), Ana (Quantaco SRE)

AutoSummary: cost/unit economics review, caching numbers looked good, need more benchmarks around cache hit ratios and batching tradeoffs, next steps agreed.

[00:00] Samira (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick check — is this still a 45 minute slot?
[00:05] Priya (Quantaco): yes, working through a tight morning but we should be good, thanks.
[00:12] Marcus (Redwood): cool, i'll kick off with the numbers we ran this week. we did two main runs: baseline streamed hosted model (fp16), and a quantized int8 variant, both with and without KV/prefix caching warm.
[00:28] Tom (Quantaco): quick question, when you say "tokens/sec/$" what's the denominator—your hosted cost assumptions or cloud gpu list price?
[00:35] Marcus (Redwood): good call — the spreadsheet uses Redwood hosted unit pricing for these POC runs (includes infra + orchestration); line items show per-hour GPU + per-request overhead, so tokens per dollar is based on total billable for that model instance. we'll send the sheet.
[00:50] Priya (Quantaco): ok, baseline numbers?
[00:55] Marcus (Redwood): baseline fp16 cold cache ~1,200 tokens/sec for a single stream, cost about $0.048 per 1k tokens so roughly $48 per million tokens. warm KV cache (prefix hits ~45%) bumped to effective 1,700 tokens/sec and reduced cost per 1M to about $33 — so ~31% savings at that hit rate.
[01:22] Ana (Quantaco): that 45% hit rate is realistic for our conversational summaries? we've only instrumented partial logs so far.
[01:30] Tom (Quantaco): yeah our current prefix reuse is probably lower, around 20-25% for user queries, but for the conversational long-term cache we expected higher for bot flows.
[01:42] Marcus (Redwood): the sensitivity runs show linear-ish improvements up to ~60% hit where batching interactions start to dominate. I should caveat that the caching gain depends on average prefix length — shorter prefixes yield smaller KV advantages.
[02:05] Samira (Redwood): did you try batching during the warm-cache runs? i remember last week there was a tail-latency spike when batch_size > 8.
[02:12] Marcus (Redwood): yes, we did three batch sizes: 4, 8, and 16. batch 4 gave the best p95 tradeoff — throughput up ~1.3x, p95 stayed under 220ms. batch 8 increased throughput 1.7x but p95 crept to ~420ms; batch 16 pushed throughput to 2.2x but p95 was 800-1,200ms depending on sequence length. so if you need low p95, avoid >8.
[02:44] Priya (Quantaco): that's helpful. our SLO for UIs is p95 < 300ms, so batch 8 is borderline. maybe batch 4 is safer for user-facing endpoints.
[02:53] Tom (Quantaco): for background jobs (rerank / batch summarization) we could leverage batch 16 to get cost down. do you have separate routing policies to route those?
[03:05] Marcus (Redwood): yep — smart routing can send background jobs to a dedicated quantized variant or to dedicated capacity pool. Dedicated pools have a different cost model but lower unit costs at high sustained throughput.
[03:18] Ana (Quantaco): any numbers on dedicated capacity? ballpark per-hour or tokens/sec/$?
[03:24] Samira (Redwood): for the POC size you gave (peak 200 rps, avg 60 rps), Dedicated could be 20-30% cheaper per token if you commit to the reserved nodes, after factoring in autoscale efficiency. but it needs a contract/commit and lead time to provision.
[03:42] Priya (Quantaco): and what about quantization quality? we saw small regressions in generation quality previously when moving to int8.
[03:50] Marcus (Redwood): agreed — int8 gives big cost wins but you need to validate on your eval prompts. our Optimize tool suggests model-by-workload configs — for generative quality-critical flows we recommend fp16 or int8 with calibration + eval-set gating. we ran a small eval and saw ~3% delta in rouge/score for long-form summarization on our test prompts.
[04:12] Tom (Quantaco): any option to do hybrid? e.g., fp16 for first-pass user-visible step and int8 for background post-processing?
[04:18] Marcus (Redwood): yes that's a recommended pattern — route interactive requests to high-quality variants and background jobs to cheap variants. it also pairs well with caching because caches feed the interactive path more.
[04:30] Priya (Quantaco): can we get a simulation where you change cache hit from 20->50->70% so we can see break-even on Dedicated vs Hosted?
[04:37] Marcus (Redwood): absolutely — that's on the benchmark plan. i'll run sensitivity across hit rates and batch sizes and include Dedicated throughput numbers.
[04:45] Ana (Quantaco): also can you include cost per 1M tokens in the sheet and separate line items: infra, orchestration, storage (for cache), and egress?
[04:53] Samira (Redwood): will do. we'll include rows for storage cost (kv cache store), and egress where applicable.
[04:58] Tom (Quantaco): do you have guidance on acceptable cache eviction TTLs or sizing? our team is concerned about memory usage on the nodes.
[05:06] Marcus (Redwood): TTL is workload-specific but for convo flows we usually see 12-48 hour TTLs with LRU/approximate eviction; for pricing the cache storage cost is modest relative to GPU time, but it does increase memory/disk footprint on the serving nodes. we can size for your projected active sessions to give concrete numbers.
[05:30] Priya (Quantaco): curious about batching tradeoffs for long sequences — your seq lengths vary a lot for our dataset, from 128 up to 2048 tokens. how does that affect tokens/sec/$?
[05:40] Marcus (Redwood): longer sequences reduce throughput nonlinearly — the kernels scale roughly O(n^2) for attention, so tokens/sec drops with longer context. we included sequence-weighted averages in the spreadsheet, but i'll attach per-length buckets. in general, batching helps more on shorter sequences.
[05:59] Samira (Redwood): any surprising anomalies in the runs?
[06:03] Marcus (Redwood): one thing was a CPU-side preproc bottleneck when batch_size=16 on the hosted node; we increased the preprocess threads and that improved end-to-end throughput but it adds CPU cost. also a few transcription mismatches in logs — small things.
[06:20] Tom (Quantaco): ok thanks — regarding security/compliance, if we go Dedicated or Private later, what changes in audit logs and KMS?
[06:28] Samira (Redwood): Dedicated includes more granular RBAC and longer retention for logs; Private gives you your own VPC and KMS/HSM integration. for the POC we can enable request-level audit logs and SSO.
[06:40] Ana (Quantaco): got it. can you also run a p99 tail-latency profile for each batch size? we care about tail for our real-time endpoints.
[06:48] Marcus (Redwood): yes p99 is in the plan — for batch 8 & 16 p99 is where we saw the biggest jumps; we'll include p50/p95/p99.
[06:58] Priya (Quantaco): what's your recommended production setup given our SLO (p95 <300ms) and target to minimize cost?
[07:06] Marcus (Redwood): recommended: interactive endpoints on fp16 with batch_size=4, warm KV cache target 40-50% (you said some flows can hit that), background workers on int8 batch 16, and evaluate Dedicated if sustained throughput >100 rps; that should hit SLOs and reduce cost by ~20-30% overall compared to hosted baseline.
[07:30] Tom (Quantaco): makes sense. Priya — do you want us to prioritize the cache-hit sensitivity benchmark or the per-length throughput buckets?
[07:36] Priya (Quantaco): cache sensitivity first, then sequence buckets. also include a scenario that shows cost if cache misses spike (worst-case).
[07:45] Samira (Redwood): good — action items recap coming. Marcus, you'll run benchmarks; i'll send the spreadsheet and Dedicated pricing examples.
[07:53] Marcus (Redwood): yep will do, uploading to the shared folder and will ping when done.
[07:58] Priya (Quantaco): will confirm QPS/SLO next week and aim to have logs for prefix reuse.
[08:05] Ana (Quantaco): i'll look at memory sizing for cache nodes and send notes.
[08:10] Samira (Redwood): perfect. any other questions?
[08:14] Tom (Quantaco): none from me.
[08:17] Priya (Quantaco): all good. thanks.
[08:20] Samira (Redwood): thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts and proposed meeting for Dedicated deep dive if needed.

Meeting close.

References/Links mentioned: updated_cost_model.xlsx (will be uploaded), benchmark CSVs (to come), Dedicated_pricing_overview.pdf (sent on request).
